name: Scaffold Running (The Unaugmented League)
description: A formally structured freerunning competition circuit that prohibits all active augmentation during runs — no chrome-assist reflexes, no BCI-paced movement, no subdermal impact dampening. Participants must disable or physically cap their augments before a certified official, then complete courses built across GLMZ's exterior scaffold networks, construction remnants, and the famous 'Rib Cage' — the exposed superstructure of a never-finished Tier 3 arcology tower in the Waukee Corridor. What began in 2209 as a protest against augmented leagues pricing out unaugmented athletes has evolved into a fiercely respected discipline, with its own aesthetic philosophy: 'bone and breath,' meaning the body as it was born. Crowds are loud, betting is heavy, and the courses are brutally difficult — designed by a collective called the Framebuilders who treat course design as architectural art.
cultural_impact: Scaffold Running has sparked a broader cultural conversation about what 'natural' means in a city where baseline humanity is increasingly rare — its 'bone and breath' philosophy has been adopted by wellness communities, anti-augmentation activists, and, ironically, by augment manufacturers as marketing language. Live events draw mixed-tier crowds and are one of the few spaces where Tier 2 and Tier 3 residents share physical space without corporate mediation.
key_figures: Damilola Kirchner-Yue (three-time circuit champion, vocal anti-augmentation advocate)
The Framebuilders (anonymous course design collective, 6-9 members)
Sable Osei-Thorvaldsen (league commissioner, former augmented athlete)
locations: The Rib Cage (unfinished arcology superstructure, Waukee Corridor)
Pilsen Scaffold District (Tier 2 construction zone, permanent course)
Harborwall North (Tier 3 elevated transit ruins, seasonal venue)
story_hooks: A runner collapses mid-course and the post-race medical scan reveals hidden augmentation — but the implant is military-grade, involuntary, and the runner has no memory of receiving it.

The Framebuilders announce a new course built inside a sealed Shelf tunnel, and the permit dispute with the corponation that owns the infrastructure becomes a flashpoint for Tier 1 land rights activists.

A Tier 5 investor offers to sponsor the league with a contract that would require all runners to wear sponsored 'passive' augments — ones that monitor biometrics and sell the data. The league is split on whether to accept.
